Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

avoid verb

also keep away from, steer clear of, shun, dodge, avoid doing, shun publicity

classical

Liv. praef. 10: inde foedum inceptū foedum exitū quod vītēs
Publ. I 20: Īrātum breviter vītēs, inimīcum diū.

vītō, vītāre, vītāvī, vītātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

avoid, keep away from

Other words

  • ēvītō, ēvītāre, ēvītāvī, ēvītātum — avoid, get out of the way of

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 88: quās tum ēvītāre, tum ēlevāre, tum ferre sapientis est; Traupman 97, 307: rem ēvītāre, to duck the issue

  • dēclīnō, dēclīnāre, dēclīnāvī, dēclīnātum — turn aside from, steer clear of

    verb, first conjugation; with an accusative, or ab and the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.145: ab iīs est dīligentius dēclīnandum

  • fugiō, fugere, fūgī, fugitum — shun, keep away from

    verb, third conjugation (-iō), transitive · also used · classical · Publ. I 43: Inertia indicātur, cum fugitur labor.

  • caveō, cavēre, cāvī, cautum — beware of, take care not to

    verb, second conjugation; with an accusative, or nē and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 324: Cavē nē cadās; Cic. Off. 1.123: nihil autem magis cavendum est senectūtī, quam nē languōrī sē dēsidiaeque dēdat

    To avoid doing something is cavē nē with the subjunctive, or cavē with the subjunctive alone. See careful, don’t fall.

Examples

  • inde tibi tuaeque reī pūblicae quod imitēre capiās, inde foedum inceptū foedum exitū quod vītēs

    From it you may take for yourself and your country what to imitate, and from it what to avoid, foul in its beginning, foul in its end.Liv. praef. 10

  • ferās, nōn culpēs, quod vītārī nōn potest

    What cannot be avoided you must bear, not blame.Gell. 17.14.4 (Publilius)

  • est enim varius et multiplex ūsus amīcitiae multaeque causae suspīciōnum offēnsiōnumque dantur, quās tum ēvītāre, tum ēlevāre, tum ferre sapientis est

    For friendship has many uses and many sides, and many causes of suspicion and offence arise, which it is the wise man’s part now to avoid, now to make light of, now to bear.Cic. Amic. 88

  • forum ac lūcem fugere

    to shun publicityTraupman 180

See also careful, don’t fall, protect.
